interest: This telegram provides vital firsthand intelligence on Japan's military build-up in southern China in July 1941, just months prior to the outbreak of the Pacific War. It highlights the strategic transformation of Hainan Island into a major forward operating staging ground for Japan's southern advance (Nanshin-ron) toward Southeast Asia and the Philippines, complete with a 100-million-yen naval base and modern air base. The document is also historically notable for showcasing the role of Everitt Groff-Smith—an American who remained in place as Commissioner of the Chinese Maritime Customs in Japanese-occupied territory—as an intelligence informant for U.S. diplomats, and it features Department of State liaison notations indicating immediate oral briefing of the Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) and Military Intelligence Division (MID).
overview: This file consists of a two-page confidential telegram (No. 235) dated July 8, 1941, sent from Hong Kong by U.S. Consul John H. Bruins to the Secretary of State in Washington, with copies repeated to Chungking, Peiping, Canton, and Tokyo. The telegram reports intelligence gathered from a private conversation with Everitt Groff-Smith, an American serving as Commissioner of the Chinese Maritime Customs on Hainan Island during a visit to Hong Kong. Groff-Smith detailed significant Japanese military construction on the occupied island, including rapid progress on a 100-million-yen naval base at the southern end designed to counterpoise American naval facilities in the Philippines, and the near completion of a one-square-mile air base with concrete runways. He additionally reported the ongoing withdrawal of the Japanese Army, which was slated to leave the Imperial Japanese Navy in exclusive control of Hainan by August 1, 1941. Department notations indicate the substance of the report was shared immediately with ONI and MID.

subfiles.about: Reports intelligence from Chinese Maritime Customs Commissioner Everitt Groff-Smith regarding Japanese naval and air base construction on Hainan Island and the impending transfer of full administrative control to the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.from: John H. Bruins (American Consulate, Hong Kong)
subfiles.summary: U.S. Consul John H. Bruins reports on a confidential conversation with Everitt Groff-Smith, the American Commissioner of the Chinese Maritime Customs on Hainan Island, visiting Hong Kong. Groff-Smith disclosed that Japan was rapidly constructing a naval base at the southern end of Hainan costing roughly 100,000,000 yen as a counterweight to U.S. bases in the Philippines, alongside a nearly completed one-square-mile air base with partial concrete surfacing. He also noted that joint Japanese Army-Navy administration was concluding, with complete Army withdrawal anticipated by August 1, 1941, placing the Navy in total command. State Department endorsements show the intelligence was orally relayed to ONI and MID on July 9, 1941.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 235 from Hong Kong (Bruins) on Japanese Naval and Air Base Construction on Hainan Island
